summary.headline: Bluspring Q2 FY27 revenue crossed ₹1,000 crore (ex-foundit ₹1,250 crore, +49% YoY), with EBITDA margin up 188 bps to 5.4%.
summary.overview: Excluding foundit, Q2 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to ₹1,250 crore, EBITDA more than doubled to ₹67 crore (margin 5.4%), and PAT grew 95% to ₹32 crore. Growth was driven by acquisitions (STEAG full quarter, LSG Sky Chefs from August 2026) plus new large energy contracts, with existing businesses growing 16% YoY. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of revenue above ₹4,700 crore, EBITDA above ₹200 crore and PAT of ₹100 crore, and said foundit is tracking to near break-even by Q4. Acquisition debt and interest cost rose sharply in the quarter.

segments.name: Smart Infra, Energy & Engineering (formerly Telecom & Industrials)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹449 crore (+189% YoY, +101% QoQ); H1 ₹672 crore (+119%). EBITDA ₹49 crore (+283% YoY), margin 10.9% (+266 bps). About ₹280 crore of Q2 revenue came from STEAG with ~₹30 crore of EBITDA; 16 contracts mobilised with ₹641 crore ACV. Telecom grew muted.

segments.name: Facility & Food Services
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹601 crore (+17% YoY, +15% QoQ); H1 ₹1,121 crore (+13%). EBITDA ₹29 crore (+38% YoY), margin 4.7% (+72 bps). Includes LSG Sky Chefs from August: ₹18 crore revenue and ₹4-5 crore EBITDA in Q2.

segments.name: Security Services
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹201 crore (+20% YoY, +7% QoQ); H1 ₹387 crore (+22%). EBITDA ₹6 crore (+27% YoY), margin about 3% (+19 bps). 20 new clients mobilised with ₹30 crore ACV.

segments.name: foundit (excluded from above figures)
segments.commentary: Q2 sales ₹30 crore, revenue ₹22 crore, EBITDA loss ₹12 crore. H1 EBITDA burn about ₹26 crore; management expects H2 burn of ₹12-13 crore, taking FY27 burn below ₹40 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reiterated: revenue above ₹4,700 crore, EBITDA above ₹200 crore, PAT of ₹100 crore. Management said EBITDA will comfortably cross ₹200 crore, with Q3 similar to Q2 and Q4 better than Q2.
Company exit annualised revenue run-rate is above ₹4,700 crore; target 6% EBITDA margin well before FY30.
Organic growth of 18-20% targeted for FY28 on the new base; medium-term 3x GDP growth (18-20%) through FY30-FY32.
Acquisition debt to fall from ~₹280-300 crore to ~₹150 crore by year-end via free cash; working-capital debt to stay ~₹150-200 crore. Management said no debt for organic businesses at closing.
Working capital days expected to settle around 40 days for FY27. Tax rate guidance of 22% for FY27 retained.
foundit to reach near break-even by Q4 FY27, requiring about ₹38-40 crore sales (₹30-33 crore revenue). Total board-approved foundit loans of ₹150 crore; about ₹106 crore lent so far.
Other expenses to stay at similar levels in H2 (Q2 ₹253 crore vs Q1 ₹108 crore, mainly STEAG subcontracting); company will report STEAG subcontracting as a separate line item.
capex_capacity: STEAG O&M presence is about 14-15 GW of thermal capacity; management cited thermal at 66% of 271 GW summer peak demand.
LSG kitchen at Bengaluru Airport under a concession to 2039 currently does ₹110-120 crore revenue at 17-18% margin; target ₹15-20% growth over two years (management phrasing).
Two acquisitions in H1 for ₹340 crore purchase consideration, mostly acquisition debt (~₹300 crore); acquired entities brought ~₹188 crore cash.
No active acquisition in the pipeline; management focus is integrating STEAG and LSG.
Management is exploring international opportunities; STEAG has an existing footprint in one African country. Wind is not in the portfolio; solar and a pipeline in wind are present.
demand_pricing: H1 new contracts with ACV above ₹900 crore added; most won by Smart Infra, Energy & Engineering. All large announced contracts are now mobilised.
Industrial sector share of revenue rose to 37%; energy and industrial share expected to exceed one-third of revenue by year-end (from one-fifth in FY26).
Top 30 clients are 53% of revenue. Workforce above 100,000, with 8,000+ added in H1 (2,800+ from acquisitions).

Management said new contracts carry 60-75 days payment terms; gross DSO is above 90 days, while net working capital is about 38 days. Unbilled revenue should hover around 35 days; only ₹11 crore is non-current unbilled revenue.
Management said LSG Sky Chefs contracts are non-exclusive: airports typically have 2-3 kitchen operators and airline contracts run 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is foundit progressing as planned, and what sales are needed to break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on plan: Q2 sales of ₹30 crore were the highest in 10+ quarters. Break-even needs about ₹30-33 crore of P&L revenue, or about ₹38-40 crore of sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the acquisition debt and what will year-end debt look like?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹300 crore of acquisition debt was raised, of which ~₹20 crore has been repaid; ~₹280 crore remains. Acquisition debt should fall to ~₹150 crore by Q4, with working-capital debt of ₹150-200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revised foundit burn and loan balance?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 burn was about ₹26 crore; H2 burn is guided at ₹12-13 crore, keeping FY27 below ₹40 crore. About ₹106 crore of the ₹150 crore board-approved loan limit has been lent. Partial exit is possible after break-even.

qa_highlights.question: What drives other expenses (₹253 crore in Q2 vs ₹108 crore in Q1)?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly STEAG subcontracting, with the rest relating to telecom subcontracting. H2 other expenses should be at similar levels; STEAG subcontracting will be reported as a separate line.

qa_highlights.question: What is STEAG's contribution and LSG's contribution in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: STEAG contributed about ₹280 crore revenue and ~₹30 crore EBITDA in Smart Infra. LSG contributed ₹18 crore revenue and ₹4-5 crore EBITDA from August.

qa_highlights.question: What are the long-term growth and margin targets, and FY27 EBITDA upside?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 EBITDA to comfortably exceed ₹200 crore and targets 18-20% organic growth in FY28. The 6% EBITDA margin target is expected to be reached before FY30.

risks_watch: Borrowing costs elevated: interest rose to ₹16 crore in Q2 from ₹8 crore in Q1, with tighter liquidity cited.
Integration risk: management bandwidth is focused on integrating STEAG and LSG; no further acquisitions in the pipeline.

Working capital: net WC days expected to rise to ~40 from 38; large new contracts add receivables and unbilled revenue. FY26 unbilled revenue rose to ₹341 crore gross from ₹163 crore in FY25 (analyst citation; flagged as a key audit matter).
foundit: one-month active users down 5% QoQ and 6-month actives flat at ~5.4 million per analyst; break-even depends on sales converting to revenue.
Tax rate: H1 ETR was about 18% per management, against the 22% FY27 guidance; analyst noted H1 ~49% and Q2 ~35% reported rates.
Telecom vertical growth muted; security margin still ~3%, below the 4-4.5% target.
Other expenses (STEAG subcontracting) are large and rising; separate disclosure from next quarter.
key_quotes: We may not be able to give you exact numbers, but we'll comfortably, basis the quarter two base, mathematically, we'll definitely cross INR 200.
But as we speak, there is no active acquisition in the pipeline.

While borrowing costs are expected to remain elevated given the prevailing macroeconomic environment and tighter liquidity conditions, our strong cash generation outlook provides confidence in our ability to accelerate debt repayment and mitigate the impact of higher financing costs.

So, foundit is exactly going as per plan. If you look at the quarterly, see this kind of business obviously there is a slight gap between when you do the sales and when you get the revenue into the P&L.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the headline numbers, FY27 guidance and foundit break-even timing, repeating these with firm language. More cautious on borrowing costs, which management said will stay elevated, and evasive on acquisition pipeline and exact FY27 EBITDA figure, declining to give precise numbers beyond "comfortably" crossing ₹200 crore.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Interest cost rose to ₹16 crore from ₹8 crore, the H1 tax rate ran about 18% against a 22% guide, and foundit needs about ₹38-40 crore of sales to break even by Q4.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launch was discussed.

rows.label: Acquisition debt halved to ~₹150 crore by Q4
rows.why: Acquisition debt of ~₹280 crore remains and management guides it to about ₹150 crore by year-end from free cash flow, while net debt is ₹126 crore on ₹320 crore cash.

rows.label: foundit near break-even by Q4 FY27
rows.why: Q2 sales of ₹30 crore were the highest in 10+ quarters, EBITDA loss narrowed to ₹12 crore from ₹14 crore, and H2 burn is guided at ₹12-13 crore, needing ₹38-40 crore of sales for break-even.

rows.label: Mobilisation of ~₹900 crore H1 ACV
rows.why: All large announced contracts are now mobilised, with 16 contracts at ₹641 crore ACV in Smart Infra alone, and Q2 revenue ex-foundit reached ₹1,250 crore (+49% YoY).

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 revenue, EBITDA and PAT guidance and foundit break-even, but cautious on borrowing costs and evasive on the acquisition pipeline and exact EBITDA figure.
